thesis: Machines can now do much of the thinking people are paid for, cheaply and on hardware a person can own, and the old deal (sell your days or you don't eat) is ending before anyone has written its replacement. In this book the Singularity is the point where intelligence stops being scarce and the institutions built on that scarcity start failing before a replacement exists. CT forecasts AGI by Thanksgiving 2027, names what would prove him wrong, and builds every ask so it still holds if he is wrong. The danger is the arrangement around the machine, not the machine: productive capacity and human security can move in opposite directions, there is already enough food, and hunger, eviction and credit gatekeeping are enforced rules that people wrote and can rewrite. We don't have to live like this. So the core gives a reader starting from zero something concrete to start this week: food first, for everyone, regardless of income or employment; then land, shelter and care; machines, land and compute owned close to home by the people who depend on them; free at the door but paid for together, like a library; money made optional, not abolished; and a public floor built rung by rung, raised by automation. It carries that argument inside a story a newcomer can feel. Elijah demos the future at a bar and helps end three careers, then spends three years being corrected by a welder, a twice-reskilled warehouse worker, a soil scientist, a hardware man and a woman with a braced wrist, and learns that the answer to the machine was never a smarter machine but people who know each other, multiplied. It ends where it began, at the Bear Flag, with the toast reclaimed and the book left on the bar, and it hands the reader one question for every automation decision, a year of practices, and a meeting to go to.

spine.idea: The robots have won the old deal: what you lose is having to sell your days to eat, and that loss is an opening (CT's April 2024 first line and its turn).
What is happening: thought itself is now automated, cheaply and on home hardware; go around the pundits and use the tools yourself.
Surviving the Singularity means keeping people fed, housed and cared for, with a say over who owns the tools; make the machines grow our food first.
The second ox: AI as a thinking draft animal people must train, feed and direct.
Fired on a Tuesday, dinner already handled: the picture of it going right.
Listen to the fear under 'AI will take my job': productive capacity and human security can move apart, so carry the gain through to the person.
We don't have to live like this: there is enough food, and scarcity is an enforced arrangement of rules people can change.
Money optional, not abolished; markets stay above the floor.
The design brief: if a robot can grow my food and build my house, why am I still renting my survival? Answered in the Conclusion.
Free at the door is not free to provide: fund it together like a library, and start feeding people while the funding is argued.
The machine is unprecedented, the stampede is not: the Precedent Ledger, kept as chapter precedents and as twenty-four one-line rules.
One demonstration, seven days, three careers, no villain: the well-meaning enthusiast becomes the accomplice, and the precarious are hit first.

The working definition: the Singularity is the point where intelligence stops being scarce and institutions built on that scarcity fail before a replacement is written; no god required, testable on your own paycheck, and the emergency is the gap.
A dated, falsifiable forecast (AGI by Thanksgiving 2027) with stated falsifiers and survey evidence; every ask holds if it is wrong.
Plan by doors, not dates: expert timelines are autopsies of the last failure; make one asymmetric bet.
Four questions hide in one word (capability, improvement, deployment, access), and this book lives in access.
Who gets the savings: the payroll incentive turns cheap thinking into hunger for specific people.
Enclosure: the builder discovers he planted the hedge; the land trust later runs enclosure in reverse.
The stages are scenarios, not a timetable; Stage 4, the new social contract, is the hinge and a decision available now.
Exponentials look like nothing, then everything; seeing it coming exiles you from the people you love; the threat was always man versus man.
Find the edge of your map and work the near end; godlike machines beside hungry people would be a failure of priorities.
Intelligence is energy, arranged: physics checks claims but never prices a person, and the ledgers stay separate.
When the cost per unit of work flips, sentiment doesn't save the incumbent (the horse and the ledger).
Capability is not access; the preservation solution adds abundance under everyone and takes nothing; ownership has to reach the terms people depend on.
Technologies spread by group advantage, not consent: spend energy on position, not on whether.
Reskilling is what the comfortable prescribe; ask where the person stands meanwhile, build the floor instead of the fence, and keep it unconditional.
The battle line runs through every person as two reflexes; when intelligence is cheap, trust from specific people is the scarce asset, so stop climbing and start weaving.
Argue about the machine's invoice, not its soul (the Music Performance Trust Fund).
Panic is a state, not information; resilience is room to move, not attitude; build a cognitive firewall; autonomy is relational, and a circle never withholds food to keep people in line.

Need the long supply chain less: design for repair, deglobalize survival needs, plan at the scale of the region, decide in advance where the saving goes, and remember interdependence is contagion in foul weather.
Create more than you consume, with nobody earning dinner; real recorded experience is now the scarce input; wrap useful knowledge in a true story and point people off the platform.
Own the compute you think on; knowing a system is not operating it; follow one request all the way through before buying a machine.

Land is the input the machine can't make; meet survival needs on your own ground or through a city that runs them better; trust closes what data can't; help arrives without condescension, starting now.
The shouse: production and shelter under one roof, built in your lane, never cutting a load-bearing member first.
Collapse is readable before it lands, so say so; efficiency is a choice about whose books show the loss; shorten the loops; recover food in the wrong place; security buys time to choose.
A meter tells the truth only where it sits; know the ground's history; distributed food production scales once somebody organizes it.
Trust doesn't scale, blueprints do: ship the files, keep consent first, own your press; leverage is reach over permission.
A tool you can't understand, repair or run offline is a leash; tools don't choose which future they serve, people do; discipline is a practice.

Run the premortem with people in it, measure by the Adequate Level of Care, build the machine and the promise together, and make whoever automates answer for the people moved out; nobody should have to be liked to be fed.
The ladder: survival as a public floor built rung by rung, food first, raised by automation; each rung stands alone; ask who it can't be afforded by and how it became free somewhere else.
Civic action that works: testimony beats the model; bring one specific request sized to the speaking limit and follow it in writing; a role for every reader.
One question for every automation decision, success measured by time returned and danger avoided, and the moral mandate.
The bookend: the toast reclaimed, the napkin redeemed, the reader holding the book.
A year of sequenced practice and the organizer's questions: the single home for what to do on Monday.

principles: Whole blocks only, verbatim. Never trim a sentence. A defect inside a block that must stay (a broken sentence, a title dash, a dangling pointer) is recorded as a seam for CT's v0.12 rewrite, not patched and not used as a reason to keep a weaker block.

Every budget is the word count of the keep list named in that file's priorities. Cutters may swap blocks of similar size inside the 8 percent band, but a swap must not break a continuity pair or bring back a dropped duplicate.

Spend in the order a newcomer needs: first understanding (the definition, the stages, the physics), then caring (Elijah, Denny, Rosa, Frank), then acting (the firewall, start with three, the premortem, the ladder, the year plan). Definitions and the floor argument outrank speculation; the plan outranks reference material.

Scenes are the engine. Keep each scene through its turn and every planted setup or payoff. Cut narration that explains a beat after it lands, captions that spoil the scene, and backstory that delays the hook.
A setup stays only if its payoff stays, and the reverse. When a pair cannot both fit, both go and the dangling reference is logged as a seam.
One home per idea, as the duplicates list names. Only Appendix C (the ten-minute hand-off) and Appendix G (the year plan) may restate the body, because restating is their job.
In the Foundations keep the claim, its single best evidence and its one concrete action. Cut stacked hedges, stat runs that bury the hammer line, and passages in a committee or policy-memo register.

Insider material goes first: the lineage beyond Good, Vinge and Kurzweil; benchmark tables; the simulation trilemma; VRAM, heat, PID and Fourier math; install scripts; Hansard detail; tax classifications; cyberdeck anatomy; Stage 7 and Stage 9 speculation.

Precedents keep their hook, mechanism and rule where they earn a place; seventeen stay (P-02, P-03, P-04, P-06, P-07, P-08, P-10, P-11, P-12, P-13, P-16, P-18, P-19, P-20, P-21, P-22, P-23). P-01, P-05, P-09, P-14, P-15, P-17 and P-24 go because they contradict their chapter, duplicate a scene or stand between the climax and the ending; all twenty-four rules survive in Appendix D b0023.
Practices live in Appendix G. A chapter keeps its own practice only when Appendix G lacks it: P-02's boring test, P-03's doors and asymmetric bet, P-06's undemotable list.

CT's voice beats committee voice. When two blocks carry one idea, keep the one closest to his April 2024 draft and his own dictated lines (for example Introduction b0050, b0147, b0148; Ch1 b0173; Ch12 b0136; Ch13 b0164; Ch19 b0096, b0105), and keep profanity that earns its place.
Apparatus goes: figures, captions, epigraphs, In this chapter bullets, interactive markers, LaTeX and code. The one exception is the Ch17 epigraph b0151, because Marta answers it in b0143.
No pointer survives to material the cut removes unless its target is kept; a pointer and its target are dropped together, and a pointer trapped inside a kept block is listed as a seam.

Get to the hook fast. Front matter (Introduction, Preface, How to Use, Chapter 0) falls from 9,236 words to 5,840; How to Use goes, the Introduction keeps its hammer lines and loses its stat run, tours and signposts, and the Preface keeps CT's first line and the horse parable.

Keep the entry bar low wherever there is a choice: blocks saying a reader can take part without land, servers or a robot (Introduction b0132, Ch5 b0158, Ch12 b0164) outrank blocks that assume ownership.
The plan writes no em or en dashes. Dashes inside kept book text (the stage-range titles of Ch2, Ch3 and Ch4) are flagged for CT, not edited.
rationale: METHOD. I rebuilt every budget from a block-level keep list instead of averaging the three proposals: for each file I merged the architects' keep and cut lists, decided each disagreement against the annotated text, summed the kept blocks' word counts, and rounded to the nearest 10 (the three dividers are exact). Each file's priorities now open with that exact keep list, so a cutter can hit the budget and knows what to cut first. ARITHMETIC. Front matter 5,840 (Introduction 2,370 + Preface 530 + How to Use 0 + Chapter 0 2,940). Part I 9,442 (divider 62 + Ch1 2,650 + Ch2 2,100 + Ch3 1,220 + Ch4 1,210 + Ch5 2,200). Part II 9,957 (divider 57 + Ch6 2,270 + Ch7 3,000 + Ch8 2,520 + Ch9 2,110). Appendix B is untouched and uncounted. THREE READERS. The newcomer gets a fast hook (CT's first line, the Bear Flag), a definition before any jargon (Ch1 keeps the definition, the four questions and the Einstein picture and loses the benchmark tables), the floor argument in story form (Denny, Rosa, Gary and Sal), and one sequenced year of actions. The reader already into the singularity gets the falsifiable forecast with its falsifiers and survey evidence, doors not dates, the stage map (compact in Appendix C), the energy physics and the ownership question. The reader looking for a different perspective gets what the genre usually lacks: the human arrangement as the real variable, enclosure run in reverse, New Communities as an honest counterweight, the Music Performance Trust Fund invoice, the county hearing, and CT's anger aimed at the arrangement, never the reader. VERDICT ON v0.11.0. Not publishable as is. The front matter runs about 9,300 words through four front doors before Chapter 1 says what the Singularity is; the Introduction and Chapter 1 define AGI two different ways; the AI-slop riff sneers at the artists Chapter 0 grieves for; most scenes are followed by narration explaining them; the Conclusion ends three times; several precedents argue against their own chapters; and Part III spends thousands of words on reference material in a hedged committee voice far from CT's April 2024 draft. Every one of those failures can be removed by dropping whole blocks, and the spine fits in about 50,000 words, which is the evidence that a strong book sits inside this one.
